candidates.exact_span: The permittee must report total or total recoverable metal concentrations for compliance purpose. Because State WQS for aluminum and copper were dissolved-based criteria, the linear partition coefficient for copper to convert dissolved copper concentration to total concentration is used to calculate the maximum daily effluent limitation. However, because a partition coefficient for aluminum is not available, the effluent limitation for total aluminum is based on the dissolved criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of whether compliance is measured as total vs dissolved metal, and whether partition-coefficient conversion applies to aluminum vs copper, would change which numeric limit is used for measurement comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Three samples with hardness data were submitted and the average of these samples 187 mg/L was used for RP screening purposes. The permit proposes to continue to include monitoring for hardness (CaCO3) for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether hardness monitoring is an applicable obligation for the evaluation period, and whether it is required only for future RP analysis, affects determination of required vs not-required monitoring.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum did show RP, however because the prescribed daily and 30 day average limit concentration (3.2 mg/l) is less stringent than the limit in the previous permit, the previous limit will be maintained at the request of NMED and to comply with antibacksliding requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of which aluminum concentration limit (3.2 mg/l vs prior permit limit) is enforceable under antibacksliding would change the applicable numeric limit for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Permit limit of 0.75 mg/l daily max was previously established for aluminum based on water quality standards. It is proposed that the permit limit of 0.75 mg/l be applied to the 30 day average.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether 0.75 mg/l applies as a daily maximum, a 30-day average, or both changes which limit type and value govern exceedance evaluation for aluminum measurements.

candidates.exact_span: Because aluminum exhibited RP, daily and 30 day loadings of 0.78 lbs/day will be established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether mass-loading limits (0.78 lbs/day) are established and applicable, in addition to concentration limits, affects which enforceable numeric limits must be compared to reported results.

candidates.exact_span: Copper did not show RP, however permit limit of .0011 mg/l daily max was previously established for copper based on water quality standards and will be maintained in the draft permit. It is proposed that this limit be applied to the 30 day average as well.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether the 0.0011 mg/l limit applies only as a daily maximum or also as a 30-day average changes the applicable copper limit for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and discharge is infrequent, dissolved copper monitoring requirements will be maintained inthe draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether dissolved copper monitoring remains required, and under what discharge-occurrence conditions, affects whether monitoring was obligated during evaluated periods.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported a non-detect result for Cadmium, however the testing submitted by the permittee did not satisfy SSM.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a non-detect result with unsatisfied SSM counts as adequate evidence, inadequate evidence, or an unresolved no-result state changes how missing-evidence cases are classified.

candidates.exact_span: As previously described the permittee has not discharged in over five years and is unable to obtain a sample to analyze at the appropriate detection level.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of a multi-year no-discharge period affects whether cadmium monitoring was required (B) and whether missing results reflect documented no-discharge, conditional non-requirement, or unresolved lack of evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: As a result, the detection limit used by the permittee .002 mg/l was used as the effluent concentration value in RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a reported detection limit may be treated as a stand-in effluent concentration for evidence purposes, versus remaining an unresolved surrogate, affects classification of presumptive or missing-evidence states.

candidates.exact_span: Using this value, cadmium showed RP and as a result limits were suggested. Only one sample result was provided as a result of a drought. Because data is limited and based on presumptive values, Cadmium monitoring and reporting requirements will be added to the draft permit to obtain more current data for later RP analysis. Limits will not be prescribed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether cadmium has any enforceable numeric limit (A), whether new monitoring/reporting is required despite absent limits (B), and whether limited drought-era sampling and presumptive values establish adequate evidence or an unresolved no-data state (C) all hinge on this passage.

candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes to continue to maintain the oil and grease narrative "no visible sheen" limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A narrative sheen standard is not an ordinary numeric discharge limit; different interpretation of its enforceability would change whether numeric compliance comparison is applicable for oil and grease.
